primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: The F2 20210G>A gain-of-function variant lies in the 3′ untranslated region and increases efficiency of 3′-end mRNA processing, increasing steady-state prothrombin mRNA and protein. Higher prothrombin availability increases thrombin generation and predisposes to venous thromboembolism.
vignette: A 28-year-old woman develops a proximal deep venous thrombosis shortly after starting an estrogen-containing oral contraceptive. Her father had a pulmonary embolism at age 42. Platelet count, prothrombin time, and activated partial thromboplastin time are normal. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous F2 20210G>A variant.
lead: Which molecular effect of this variant most directly increases her risk of venous thrombosis?
correct: More efficient processing of the 3′ end of F2 mRNA, increasing prothrombin synthesis and thrombin generation
distractors: Resistance of activated factor V to proteolytic inactivation by activated protein C
Reduced hepatic synthesis of antithrombin, decreasing inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa
Failure of endothelial thrombomodulin to activate protein C after binding thrombin
Reduced plasmin generation because tissue plasminogen activator cannot bind fibrin
distractor_notes: Activated-protein-C resistance is the mechanism of factor V Leiden, not the F2 20210G>A variant.
Inherited antithrombin deficiency can predispose to venous thrombosis by reducing inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa, but it is not caused by the F2 20210G>A variant.
Thrombomodulin-protein C signaling is an anticoagulant pathway, but F2 20210G>A does not cause thrombophilia by preventing thrombomodulin-mediated protein C activation.
Impaired fibrinolysis can be prothrombotic, but the prothrombin 20210 variant acts by increasing prothrombin expression and thrombin generation rather than by blocking tPA-fibrin binding.
key_expl: The prothrombin 20210G>A variant is located in the 3′ untranslated region of F2. It increases the efficiency and accuracy of 3′-end mRNA processing, leading to accumulation of F2 mRNA and increased synthesis of prothrombin. The resulting increase in prothrombin availability promotes greater thrombin generation and a hypercoagulable state. PT and aPTT can remain normal because these screening assays are not designed to detect this inherited tendency toward excess thrombin generation.
objective: Explain prothrombin G20210A thrombophilia as a 3′-untranslated-region gain-of-function variant that increases prothrombin expression and thrombin generation.
clues: estrogen exposure as an acquired trigger
